claim: If an EKS cluster is at or later than the platform version listed in the Prerequisites for its Kubernetes version, AWS recommends creating access entries to give IAM principals access, and recommends migrating any entries you added to the aws-auth ConfigMap to access entries; a cluster whose platform version is earlier than that version must use the aws-auth ConfigMap.

values.display: we recommend that you use this option
migrate those entries to access entries

qualifiers.condition: access entries recommended when the cluster platform version is at or later than the version in the Prerequisites; earlier platform versions must use the aws-auth ConfigMap

evidence.quote: Creating access entries** – If your cluster is at or later than the platform version listed in the [Prerequisites](access-entries.md) section for your cluster’s Kubernetes version, we recommend that you use this option.

If your cluster’s platform version is at or later than the platform version listed in the [Prerequisites](access-entries.md) section for your cluster’s Kubernetes version, and you’ve added entries to the `ConfigMap`, then we recommend that you migrate those entries to access entries.

Adding entries to the `aws-auth` `ConfigMap` ** – If your cluster’s platform version is earlier than the version listed in the [Prerequisites](access-entries.md) section, then you must use this option.
